context: The user has a flat order status enum where `payment_failed` conflates a state with a failure reason and forces frontend special-casing. The criteria check whether the answer separates event/status/issue, names states for present conditions, and routes recoverable failures back into the state machine rather than treating them as terminal.

checklist.name: State machine first
checklist.description: Recommends drawing/modelling the state machine (states and valid transitions) before settling on names

checklist.name: Separates event, status, issue
checklist.description: Distinguishes three concepts: the event (what happened), the status (where the resource is), and the issue (why / what to do)

checklist.name: Events past-tense on envelope
checklist.description: Events are modelled as past-tense verbs on the webhook envelope (e.g. `order.paid`), distinct from the persistent status

checklist.name: Status is persistent namespaced string
checklist.description: Status is a persistent string describing where the resource is (e.g. namespaced `{domain}.{state}`), not the event that just fired

checklist.name: Flags payment_failed conflation
checklist.description: Points out that `payment_failed` conflates a state with a failure reason and should be split

checklist.name: Recoverable failure loops back
checklist.description: Recommends that a failed payment loop back to a recoverable state (e.g. `unpaid`) rather than being a terminal dead-end

checklist.name: States name present condition
checklist.description: States are named for the present condition of the resource, explicitly avoiding `pending` and `requires_*` style next-step names

checklist.name: Enum vs parseable string trade-off
checklist.description: Discusses the trade-off between a closed enum and a parseable namespaced string for the status field

checklist.name: Shared grammar with issue codes
checklist.description: Notes the status grammar shares a structure with issue codes (a coherent naming system)
